description: This line plot compares the performance of two methods, ST-ES and Random, as measured by the minimum FDE20 metric, across varying numbers of examples. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," is linear and ranges from 0 to 8, with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled "minFDE20 (←)", is also linear and spans from 0.21 to 0.24, with tick marks at intervals of 0.001. The ST-ES method is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style, while the Random method is shown as an orange line with circular markers and a solid line style. At the start of the x-axis (0 examples), the ST-ES line begins at a value of 0.24 and rapidly declines to 0.210 at 2 examples, remaining relatively stable around 0.210 until 4 examples, where it dips to 0.209, then gradually rises to 0.211 at 8 examples. The Random line begins at 0.230 at 0 examples, fluctuates slightly downward to 0.222 at 2 examples, then remains relatively stable around 0.222–0.224 until 8 examples, where it ends at 0.227.
